lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The phone, email, and website look like placeholder contact details.
items.because: A placeholder website can make the résumé look unfinished.

items.says: The expected Ph.D. completion date and candidate status need to be current.
items.because: They should be updated if your status or expected date has changed.

items.says: Keeping the store within its labour budget describes a responsibility rather than a result or your contribution.
items.because: The bullet needs evidence of scope or impact.

items.says: The labour-budget detail may not earn space on a quant-focused résumé.
The unsold-bread comparison lacks a time period and a definition of how the percentage was calculated.
items.because: Without them, the 12% to 7% figure is hard to evaluate.

items.says: It is unclear whether production or demand changed and whether the reduction is attributable to your actions.
items.because: Those factors affect how the result should be evaluated.

items.says: The 35% improvement does not define “risk-adjusted returns” or explain its calculation.
items.because: As written, it is difficult to compare with the later Sharpe-ratio claims.

items.says: The validation claim needs more detail on the split design, embargo length, and protection against leakage during feature and parameter selection.
items.because: Those choices are part of the research process, not just the final backtest.

items.says: The claim that every decision used only information available at the time is absolute.
items.because: The entire research process must support it.

items.says: Your individual contribution and what “reused” means are unclear.
The point-in-time joins do not explain how timestamp alignment was handled.
It is unclear whether the feature store was a maintained system or a research pipeline.
The wording does not clearly distinguish approval, an allocation actually being made, and measured live performance.
items.because: It could be read as though the strategy was already running live.

items.says: The best Sharpe from 400 backtested configurations is reported as the expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the best result creates selection bias; that backtested Sharpe is not, by itself, an estimate of live Sharpe.

items.says: The Sharpe figures need a defined measure, baseline, annualization, and accounting of costs.
items.because: The result cannot be evaluated clearly without them.

items.says: The signal and 18-month result appear to overlap with the Kaggle project.
items.because: The ownership and timeline should be consistent rather than presenting one result as separate accomplishments.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker raises a concern about the study’s statistical independence.
items.because: Depending on the setup, identical seeds can produce duplicate or correlated random streams.

items.says: The variance-bound comparison needs its assumptions and the meaning of “tightens the previous bound by a log factor” clarified.
Your contribution and the paper’s status need to remain distinct and precise.
items.because: “Under review” is appropriate only while that is still the paper’s status.

items.says: The teaching bullet may be less central for industry quant roles.
items.because: Your research results may be more relevant if space is limited.

items.says: The package lacks a way to verify it, if one is available.
The source and time period for the 3,000 downloads need to be clear.
items.because: Total downloads should not be confused with unique users.

items.says: The bullet does not specify which parts of the package you built.
The 7% QLIKE improvement needs an aggregation method across indices and an evaluation period.
The model’s comparison with HAR-RV needs comparable data, tuning, and forecast protocols.
items.because: The comparison is meaningful only under comparable conditions.

items.says: The test setup, dependence assumptions, and definition of the crisis periods need clarification.
“Held at the 5% level” needs to accurately describe the corrected results across indices.
The feature-engineering and gradient-boosting description is too general to show your contribution.
The competition bullet lacks context or a verifiable team result.
items.because: Otherwise, it takes space without adding much evidence.

items.says: Changing to time-grouped folds does not establish that validation leakage was actually removed.
items.because: It may reduce leakage risk, but the original gap’s cause is not explained.

items.says: The 0.02 gap does not say what the number measures.
The bullet should not imply the leaderboard was a clean test set if it influenced model choices.
The order-book signal and 18-month result appear to duplicate the Northpeak claim.
items.because: Without a clear provenance and division of contributions, repeating them can look like double-counting.

items.says: Kafka lacks a concrete use elsewhere on the résumé.
items.because: Nothing else currently supports the claim.

items.says: “time-series econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: Typos are especially noticeable in a short skills section.

items.says: The listed methods may need to be more specific and supported elsewhere on the résumé.
items.because: Each should be specific enough for an interviewer to test.
